items.title: Govt unveils offer for sale to dilute LIC stake
items.description: The Centre has announced an Offer for Sale in Life Insurance Corporation of India.  This issue will open for non-retail investors on Tuesday and retail investors on Wednesday.  The divestment includes a base offer of 2.5% with an additional 4% greenshoe option.  The floor price for the Offer for Sale is fixed at ₹382 per share.  This move aids the insurer in meeting minimum public shareholding norms ahead of schedule.

items.title: These large-caps have ‘strong buy’ & ‘buy’ recos and an upside potential of more than 20%
items.description: It was after quite some time that market breadth, always a better indicator of underlying sentiment, was positive for a few trading sessions in a row. This is what needs to be watched, rather than the movement of the Nifty or Sensex. In fact, for the next few sessions, it is critical to look at market breadth because the indices will give confusing signals, especially at the start and end of each session.

items.title: Promoter ownership climbs to two-year high despite persistent FII selling
items.description: Indian promoters significantly boosted their stock purchases in the June quarter. This action drove their ownership in listed companies to a two-year peak. Meanwhile, foreign institutional investors reduced their holdings to a fourteen-year low. Domestic investors absorbed much of the foreign sell-off, reaching an all-time high. This trend highlights growing domestic participation in Indian equity markets.

items.title: Stocks in news: Paytm, LIC, Airtel, BSE, and ONGC
items.description: Markets extended gains on Monday, driven by easing oil prices and strong quarterly earnings.  Paytm's parent company sees investors selling shares worth up to Rs 2,002 crore.  The government will offer shares in LIC to non-retail investors starting Tuesday.  Airtel, ONGC, and BSE will announce their first quarter results today.  ONGC's petroleum facility will reserve half its capacity for strategic reserves.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Indian market began the week with strong momentum and expects continued positive sentiment. Encouraging first-quarter earnings and easing crude oil prices are supporting this upward trend. Investors will closely watch the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy meeting for further market direction. Developments in the US-Iran conflict and ongoing earnings season also remain key focus areas. Foreign portfolio investors and domestic institutional investors showed net buying activity on Friday.

items.title: New closing auction triggers confusion, sparks late Nifty swings
items.description: Market participants faced confusion during the new auction system's debut.  Indices and stock values diverged significantly, catching traders by surprise.  The new system determines closing prices through a separate auction process.  This change aims to create more robust closing prices for derivatives.  Tuesday's derivatives expiry will be a key test for the new system.

items.title: Stock Radar: Hero MotoCorp stock breaks out from a Flag pattern; time to buy?
items.description: Hero MotoCorp has broken out of a bullish Flag pattern on weekly charts, supported by strong volumes, positive technical indicators and sector strength. Analysts expect the stock to climb towards Rs 5,820 in the coming months, with a stop-loss at Rs 5,170.

items.title: Credit to tech infrastructure sector doubles in two years
items.description: Bank loans for India's technology infrastructure sector have doubled in two years. This growth reflects India's position as a global hub for data centers. Loans to IT services and digital infrastructure rose significantly year on year. This expansion is driven by data centers, GCCs, and IT enabled services. These segments are now showing robust growth in bank credit.
